pulse.text: **GPT-5.6's clock is slipping** — with no ship over the weekend, Polymarket's odds for an OpenAI flagship by June 30 eased to **65%** (from 78% at the last sweep), and even the July-31 line softened to **91%** (June 23 sits at just 6.5%). No new model shipped anywhere in the last 12 hours, so the frontier is unchanged: **Claude Opus 4.8** still leads (AA-Index **56** on the v4.1 scale, ahead of GPT-5.5 at 55 and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 46), and Polymarket still prices **Anthropic near 95%** to own the best model at end of June. The live stories stay the talent war and the export fight — AlphaFold laureate **John Jumper** is leaving DeepMind for Anthropic (CNBC, Jun 19), days after Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer went Google→OpenAI, while **Fable 5 and Mythos 5 remain offline** nine days into the US export freeze, now reportedly gated behind a new biometric-ID check for foreign access. On the research side, a fresh **Nature benchmark found humans still beat frontier AI on the hardest unseen math** (Jun 12). Watch the next few days for GPT-5.6 finally landing — or the June-30 window closing on it.
